why: 'doomed' covers only bad outcomes (as the note itself says); not a true synonym of the general sense
'subject' as an adjective is obscure for learners and a weak opposite
'distantly' does not mean remotely in this sense (you can't 'work distantly'); 'locally' is a forced opposite; real opposite is in person/on-site
'uninterruptedly' is far rarer than the headword; learners won't recognize it
'The rise in ticket prices was minimized by lower costs' also fits the cloze sensibly
'led the detective to reckon that...' fits the cloze; reckon is a near-synonym (think/judge)
'rejection' means refusing, not stating something is untrue
'unlikelihood' is a rare, forced form
singular 'good' reads as the adjective to learners; 'goods' is the noun in use
'image' and 'symbol' are not synonyms of metaphor (a symbol is a different device)

set.def: strong disagreement or arguing between people about something

why: 'angry' overstates it; a 'point of contention' need not be angry (WordNet: strong disagreement)
'had become so insecure that she barely spoke to anyone' also fits the cloze
'likely' is not a synonym here ('likely students/buyers' is not used)
'striking' means eye-catching, not large and awe-inspiring
near-opposites of definitive (a vague/disputed answer vs a definitive one) - breaks the opposite question
'The palace was memorable, with golden ceilings' fits the cloze sensibly
'an agency created to probe banks' fits the cloze sensibly
'The bank will coordinate an investigation' fits the cloze sensibly
'nominate' means to propose someone as a candidate, not to officially place them in the job
'She shares an office with a mentor from the sales team' fits the cloze
'simplicity' is not a synonym of clarity
greed's def (selfish wish for more) overlaps temptation's def (strong wish for something you should not have) in the def-matching questions
'suddenly' is not a synonym (unexpected need not be sudden); 'dramatically won the debate, surprising everyone' fits the cloze
robust/thorough are near-opposites (a robust/thorough study vs a flawed one); mistaken is a near-synonym (a mistaken/flawed argument)

'The new hospital will adapt/modify robots to deliver medicine' both fit the cloze sensibly
'outburst' is used of emotion or noise, not disease or war breaking out
'instinct' is an inborn tendency, not a sudden wish
'Gas prices swung sharply' fits the cloze naturally; steadily is a near-opposite of wildly
'punctual' describes people arriving on time, not well-timed actions or warnings

why: 'an utter success' is unnatural; utter is used mainly with negative or emotion nouns (utter chaos, utter surprise)
profound's def ('very great, deep, or intense') overlaps immense ('extremely large in degree') - near-synonym
naive is a near-opposite of refined/sophisticated
'constantly' means all the time, not at an even rate

'Investigators were sent to clarify the cause of the collapse' fits the cloze sensibly
'one of the most splendid moments of Olga's life' fits the cloze
'writing' and 'text' are not synonyms of prose (poetry is also writing/text); no true one-word synonym
'statesmanship' is a statesman's skill in government, not talks between nations; also too rare for level 2
'disreputable' means not respected/shady, not famous for something bad
